# EX09: Data Analysis for Continuous Improvement

## Project Summary

For my EX09 project, I analyzed whether COMP110 should add optional pre-lecture videos before class. I chose this idea because the course survey includes a direct question asking students whether optional pre-lecture videos would be helpful for their learning.

My analysis looked at overall student support for pre-lecture videos and compared that support with course difficulty, prior programming experience, and student understanding. This helped me explore whether pre-lecture videos could be especially useful for students who find the course difficult, feel less confident, or have less prior programming experience.

## Idea Being Analyzed

The course should add short optional pre-lecture videos before each class because they would help students preview difficult topics before lecture and come to class more prepared. This would create value for students, especially students who are newer to programming or who find the course pace challenging.

## Analysis

The data is useful because the survey directly asks students whether optional pre-lecture videos would be helpful for their learning. This makes the analysis closely connected to the proposed course improvement.

The first visualization gives an overall picture of student support. If many responses are on the higher end of the scale, that suggests students would likely value optional pre-lecture videos. The second visualization connects this support to course difficulty, which is important because students who find COMP110 more difficult may benefit from seeing concepts before lecture. The third visualization connects support to prior programming experience, which helps show whether students with less background knowledge may especially benefit from extra preparation.

Overall, the analysis suggests that optional pre-lecture videos could be a helpful course improvement because they would give students another way to prepare without replacing the current course structure.

## Conclusion

Based on my analysis, I recommend that COMP110 consider adding short optional pre-lecture videos before class. The survey data is relevant because students directly rated whether pre-lecture videos would be helpful for their learning.

This idea could create value by helping students preview difficult concepts before lecture and come to class more prepared. It may be especially helpful for students who find the course difficult or have less prior programming experience.

There are still possible costs and trade-offs. Creating useful videos would take time from the instructional staff, and some students may not watch them if they are optional. There is also a risk that students could feel like the course has extra work if the videos are not clearly framed as optional support.

A good refinement would be to make the videos short, focused, and limited to the hardest topics. In the future, the course could collect more data by asking whether students actually watched the videos and whether the videos helped them feel more prepared for lecture, quizzes, and programming assignments.
